items.title: Sterlite Tech up 4.92% after Q2; CLSA Outperform Rs 1,610, Nomura Buy Rs 1,350
items.text: Sterlite Technologies closed 4.92% higher at Rs 869.80 on the BSE on 26 October, after opening at Rs 799, following its Q2 FY27 results. CLSA has an 'Outperform' with a target of Rs 1,610 (46% upside) and Nomura a 'Buy' with Rs 1,350 (25.5% upside), per Moneycontrol. Broker support after the record order book keeps the stock the sector's re-rating bellwether.

items.title: Sterlite Tech Q2 FY27 PAT Rs 517 cr, revenue Rs 2,529 cr; order book record Rs 35,274 cr
items.text: Sterlite Technologies reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 2,529 crore (up about 145% from Rs 1,034 crore), EBITDA of Rs 846 crore and PAT of Rs 517 crore versus Rs 4 crore a year earlier. Profit includes a one-time net gain of Rs 161 crore from a US tariff refund. The order book reached a record Rs 35,274 crore (from Rs 18,618 crore at Q1) and the company is described as net debt-free. A US jury verdict against subsidiary Sterlite Technologies Inc. is a flagged risk, under appeal. It confirms the data-centre fibre upcycle is feeding through to earnings at India's most re-rated name.

items.title: HFCL MD: data centres ~70% of fibre cable order book; order book nearly Rs 29,000 cr
items.text: In a BusinessToday interview, HFCL MD Mahendra Nahata said data centres make up about 70% of its fibre optic cable order book, with total order book almost Rs 29,000 crore, of which about Rs 19,000 crore is fibre cable. He said China Mobile and China Telecom tenders total about 150 million fibre-km, which could absorb China's manufacturing capacity, and fibre-guided drones add an estimated 70-100 million fibre-km of demand. He cited fibre prices of about $13, up from about $1.80 roughly 18 months ago, and said the preform project should improve raw-material security and margins.

items.title: HFCL Q2 FY27 profit up 448% to Rs 394 cr; order book above Rs 28,900 cr
items.text: HFCL reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 2,541.79 crore (+143.62% YoY) and PAT of Rs 394.22 crore (+448.14%). EBITDA was Rs 658 crore at a 25.89% margin, up 640 bps YoY. The order book exceeds Rs 28,900 crore (Q1: Rs 26,665 cr), and management guides to at least 80% FY27 revenue growth and about Rs 1,800 crore of fibre, cable and preform capex. The shares rose 5% to Rs 268.81 on 19 Oct, reinforcing the read-through that fibre demand is converting into earnings for Indian makers.

items.title: Vindhya Telelinks hits 52-week high of Rs 2,995.5 as Sensex falls 0.66%
items.text: Vindhya Telelinks rose 7.72% to an intraday high of Rs 2,995.5 on 12 Oct 2026, a 52-week high, while the Sensex fell 0.66%. MarketsMojo attributes it to technical factors and cites no company announcement. The stock is up 113.46% year to date and 116.24% over one year, so the small-cap specialty-cable name has re-rated sharply, which narrows the 'still early' argument for it.

items.title: Sterlite Tech crosses Rs 1,000, record Rs 1,046.90; Nomura, Nuvama targets cited
items.text: Sterlite Technologies rose 4.80% to Rs 1,001.25 on 6 Oct, hitting an intraday record of Rs 1,046.90; it is up 454% in six months and 920% in 2026, with market cap at Rs 53,667 crore and RSI at 75.3 (overbought). Nomura has Buy with a Rs 1,350 target, citing a data-centre-led optical fibre cable demand supercycle; Nuvama has Outperform with a Rs 1,310 target and raised FY27 EBITDA estimates by 8%. Nirmal Bang's initiation (already published) projects fibre volumes rising from 32 to 68 million fibre-km by FY29.

items.title: Nirmal Bang initiates Sterlite Tech at Buy, Rs 1,340 target; stock hits record Rs 989.70
items.text: Per Univest's report, Nirmal Bang initiated coverage of Sterlite Technologies with a Buy rating and a Rs 1,340 target, about 35% upside from the 5 October close. Whalesbook reports the shares hit a record Rs 989.70 and market cap passed Rs 50,000 crore, with the stock up roughly 875% year to date. Univest puts the P/E at about 65x on annualised Q1 profit and notes contract values are estimates that depend on periodic purchase orders. The call shows broker coverage widening after the $1.2 bn hyperscaler deal, but valuation is already stretched.

items.title: HFCL rallies 12.59% in a week with three straight 5% upper circuits
items.text: HFCL rose from Rs 211.35 to Rs 237.95 between 28 Sep and 1 Oct 2026, hitting the 5% upper circuit on 29 Sep, 30 Sep and 1 Oct, while the Sensex fell 3.20%. It had dropped 3% on 28 Sep to an intraday low of Rs 200.80 on a weak BSE Telecom index. Volume on 1 Oct was 9.21 million shares, but later delivery volumes fell, which MarketsMojo reads as more speculative trading. The move shows how volatile the heavily re-rated fibre names remain.
